title: Severe cutaneous adverse drug reactions: SJS/TEN and DRESS (India)

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults and children with drug rashes in India, focused on the severe reactions — Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS), toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN) and drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) — with first steps for milder maculopapular rashes and fixed drug eruptions. Built entirely on the ICMR Cutaneous Adverse Drug Reactions workflows, Parts A and B (July 2022).
findings: Reaction types and timelines, red flags, culprit drugs, investigations, management of maculopapular rash and fixed drug eruption, drug provocation rules and allergy documentation checked against ICMR cADR STW Part A (July 2022).

SJS/TEN features and body-surface-area classification, skin, mouth and eye care, antibiotics, steroid and cyclosporine doses, referral at over 10% detachment, SCORTEN and mortality table, and DRESS features and treatment checked against ICMR cADR STW Part B (July 2022).
Part A gives two prednisolone durations for severe maculopapular rash (5–7 days and 3–5 days); both are shown.
unverifiedSections: The ICMR STW does not say whether steroids or cyclosporine is preferred in SJS/TEN; steroids are listed first and shown as preferred.
Cyclosporine dose for DRESS (second line, tertiary care) is not given; specialist dosing.
Intravenous immunoglobulin and etanercept are not covered by the ICMR STWs and are not included.
Fluid volumes for skin failure are not given in the opened sources.
Drug cautions and contraindications without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.
US labels (DailyMed) were used where Indian sources give no dose; confirm against the Indian product label (CDSCO) and hospital formulary.

pathophysiology.summary: Cutaneous adverse drug reactions (cADR) range from common, self-limiting maculopapular rashes to life-threatening SJS/TEN and DRESS. SJS/TEN is a T-cell-mediated reaction in which keratinocytes die and the epidermis detaches, usually 4 days to 2 weeks after a new drug, with painful mucosal erosions. DRESS appears later (2–12 weeks) with fever, widespread rash, facial swelling, eosinophilia, lymph node enlargement and liver, kidney or heart involvement. The most important step in every case is to stop all suspect drugs at once and refer severe reactions early (ICMR STW).
keyMechanisms: Drug-specific cytotoxic T cells trigger widespread keratinocyte death and epidermal detachment (SJS/TEN).
Loss of skin barrier causes fluid and protein loss, hypothermia and sepsis — 'skin failure'.
DRESS combines drug hypersensitivity with herpesvirus reactivation, driving eosinophilia and organ inflammation.
High-risk drugs: aromatic anticonvulsants, allopurinol, nevirapine, abacavir, co-trimoxazole, dapsone (ICMR STW).

symptoms: Fever, sore eyes, painful mouth before or with the rash (SJS/TEN)
Painful, tender skin; blisters and peeling (ICMR STW)
DRESS: fever above 38°C, widespread itchy rash, face swelling 2–12 weeks after starting a drug (ICMR STW)
physicalSigns: Dusky red macules and atypical targets with central blistering (ICMR STW)
Epidermal detachment; mucosal erosions of mouth, eyes, genitals
DRESS: rash over 50% of body surface, facial oedema, lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly (ICMR STW)
Fixed drug eruption: dusky violaceous plaques at the same site on re-exposure (ICMR STW)
redFlags: Mucosal involvement, purpuric or bullous lesions, skin tenderness, facial or acral oedema, erythroderma (ICMR STW)
High-grade fever, jaundice or reduced urine output (ICMR STW)
Detachment over 10% of body surface: refer to a centre with an intensive care unit (ICU) experienced in skin failure (ICMR STW)
Sepsis, shock or systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS): ICU (ICMR STW)
DRESS with severe liver, kidney or heart involvement (ICMR STW)
precipitants: New drug in the previous 4 weeks (ICMR STW)
Polypharmacy; recently added drugs or dose increases (ICMR STW)
Concurrent viral infection, including HIV (ICMR STW)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Superficial peeling without mucosal involvement; often children (ICMR STW).
Chronic course; direct immunofluorescence positive (ICMR STW).
Fever and prodrome before rash; no new drug (ICMR STW).
Eschar or fever pattern; Kawasaki in children (ICMR STW).
Well-defined dusky plaques; can mimic TEN when numerous (ICMR STW).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: SJS/TEN by detachment (ICMR STW Part B)
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: SJS under 10% of body surface; SJS-TEN overlap 10–30%; TEN 30% or more; TEN without spots 10% or more.

One point each: age over 40; heart rate over 120; cancer; detachment over 10%; urea over 60 mg/dL; bicarbonate under 20 mmol/L; glucose over 252 mg/dL. Mortality: 0–1 3%; 2 12%; 3 35%; 4 58%; 5 or more over 90%.
High-risk drug; fever over 38°C; rash (over 50% of body surface, facial oedema, desquamation); eosinophilia; lymphadenopathy; liver or kidney dysfunction; onset 2–6 weeks (up to 12).
Anaphylaxis 5–15 minutes; maculopapular rash, SJS/TEN and first fixed drug eruption a few hours to 2 weeks; DRESS 4–12 weeks.

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Supports diagnosis (ICMR STW Part A); monitor weekly in DRESS (Part B).

clinicalManagement.title: Stop the drug
actions: Withdraw all suspect drugs at once, except non-suspect life-saving drugs (ICMR STW).
Keep every drug taken in the last 4 weeks on the suspect list (ICMR STW).
Assess vital signs; stabilise; fluids and nutrition (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: SJS/TEN care
actions: Skin: dilute potassium permanganate, saline or chlorhexidine baths; leave detached skin in place under non-adherent vaseline gauze; topical mupirocin or fusidic acid on raw areas (ICMR STW).
Mouth: chlorhexidine rinse 2–3 times daily, soft paraffin to lips, steroid mouthwash (ICMR STW).
Systemic adjuvant therapy ideally within 24–72 hours of onset (ICMR STW).
Detachment over 10%: refer to a centre with ICU experienced in skin failure (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Infection
actions: Broad-spectrum antibiotics covering staphylococci, streptococci and Pseudomonas; adjust to cultures; avoid the suspect drug class (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: DRESS care
actions: Primary care: stop the drug, antihistamines and emollients, refer; do not add unnecessary new drugs (ICMR STW).
Monitor CBC, liver and kidney function at least weekly (ICMR STW).
Severe liver, kidney or heart involvement: tertiary multidisciplinary intensive care; cyclosporine second line if renal function is normal (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: After recovery
actions: Record the reaction, educate the patient and give an allergy card (ICMR STW).
Do not re-challenge in DRESS unless unavoidable; no provocation in active illness or pregnancy (ICMR STW).
Long-term follow-up for eye, skin and lung complications after TEN (ICMR STW).

medicationPlan.note: All doses are from the ICMR cADR STWs Parts A and B (July 2022). Systemic therapy for SJS/TEN works best within 24–72 hours; the STW lists steroids and cyclosporine without ranking them. IVIg and etanercept are not in the ICMR STW. Antibiotics only for sepsis or secondary infection, guided by culture and avoiding the culprit drug class. Not clinically reviewed.

learningObjectives: Recognise SJS/TEN and DRESS red flags.
Give first care and refer correctly.
keyPoints: Stop every suspect drug at once.
Mucosal involvement, skin pain or blisters: think SJS/TEN.
Over 10% detachment: refer to a skin-failure ICU.
DRESS appears weeks later with fever, eosinophilia and organ involvement.
pitfalls: Adding new drugs (including antibiotics of the same class) during the reaction.

patientEducation: Carry an allergy card naming the drug (ICMR STW).
Never take the drug, or related drugs, again without specialist advice.
Tell every doctor and pharmacist about the reaction.
lifestyleAndDiet: Soft, cool foods while the mouth heals
Emollients for dry, peeling skin (ICMR STW)
mdtReferrals: ICU for over 10% detachment, sepsis or shock (ICMR STW)
Hepatology, nephrology or cardiology for DRESS organ involvement
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review fixed drug eruption at 1 week (ICMR STW); DRESS: weekly blood tests during steroid taper; long-term eye, skin and lung follow-up after TEN (ICMR STW).
